newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up on crusher demand, short cover.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up on crusher demand, short cover.

text.p: Winnipeg Commodity Exchange canola closed higher on local short covering and crusher demand, traders said.
"Crushers bought 300 November. UGG and RBC-DS bought at the close, there were hedges at the high end of the trade," a trader said.
November WCE canola crush profit margin fell to -18.06 Friday from -17.38 Thursday. Sep-Nov spread $2-$1.50.
November canola rose $2.10 to close at $361.80 and January was up $1.80 at $365.30. November flax rose $3.90 to $302.20 on local and commercial demand.
November canola spread to November flax from $61 to $60.
Commercials bought October peas down US$0.60 at US$167.50.
Commission houses sold October western barley down $1.40 at $133.10 and December fell $1.40 to $135.20 as locals sold. About 100 Oct-Dec spread at $2. Volume was 775 lots.
October feed wheat fell $1.90 to $157.60, December down $2 at $157.50 with UGG the best seller, a trader said. Volume was 340 lots. Oats did not trade.
(All values in Canadian dollars per tonne except oats, feed peas.)
